conviction_note: Fundamentals lean modestly positive: the Q2 revenue bar sits on a company guide of mid-30s growth that includes Rhode's Sephora Europe pipeline fill, and the FY27 guide arithmetic leaves room for a raise. Positioning leans the other way: the stock is up ~26% since the August print, sits 0.6% under its 52-week high, carries +27 vol points of put skew, and sold a beat-and-raise in Feb 2026 (-9.18%). The findings sum to -2.0 because the positioning finding is the largest single item. The scaled number is smaller (p_up 48 on a 12.5% absolute move = -0.5) because the sign of the guide is genuinely balanced. Both numbers say direction is close to a coin flip on a large move.
bar: Revenue: about $467-471M for fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ended 2026-09-30). Sources: Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-27, $470.6M, +36.8% y/y (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand); aggregators at $466.8-468.0M (https://www.opencapital.sh/stocks/elf/earnings/q2-2026, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/ELF). These agree with the company's own Q2 guide of 'total net sales growth in the mid-30s' on a $343.9M base, about $457-471M (Q1 FY27 call, 2026-08-05: https://investor.elfbeauty.com/~/media/Files/E/ELF-IR/documents/event-and-presentation/elf-q1-fy27-earnings-call-transcript.pdf). The revenue bar is therefore sourced. Adjusted EPS: DISPUTED. Earnings Whispers gives $0.61 consensus and a $0.73 whisper, and TipRanks gives about EUR 0.50 (about $0.58). Other aggregators give $0.34-0.35. Management guided mid-teens adjusted EBITDA margins for Q2-Q4 while it reinvests the $50M tariff refund. Findings that depend on EPS are capped small. FY27 guide: net sales $1,938-1,968M (+18-20%), adjusted EBITDA $401-407M, adjusted EPS $3.50-3.55 (https://investor.elfbeauty.com/stock-and-financial/press-releases/landing-news/2026/08-05-2026-210618204). Pre-raise FY consensus was $3.33 EPS on $1.86B revenue. No current FY consensus was found.
positioning_check: Short interest was 4.39M shares as of the 2026-10-15 FINRA data, 3.5 days to cover on 1.24M average daily volume; that is about 7.4% of the 59.01M shares outstanding (my calculation). It was up from 4.11M and 3.1 DTC on 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/elf, page as of 2026-11-04), and down from 7.64M (13.4%) on 2026-07-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/elf-beauty-nyseelf-short-interest-down-362-in-july-2026-07-30/). This is not a crowded short, so a squeeze is a minor mechanism. Options (sealed baseline): 25-delta skew is +26.97 vol points, so downside is heavily paid. Event-implied move is 11.62% and the put/call OI ratio is 0.27 on thin OI of 5,669. Tape: +11.96% over 20 days, +1.89% over 5 days, 0.59% below the 52-week high and +137% off the 52-week low.

findings.finding: Q2 revenue is set up for a beat on a bar the company itself set. Management guided Q2 total net sales growth in the mid-30s (about $457-471M on a $343.9M base), explicitly including pipeline shipments for rhode's Sephora Europe launch. The CEO said 'all that pipeline is going to go out in Q2' and that they were 'taking an even stronger stance on the pipeline' given prior Rhode launches. Rhode launched on 2026-09-30 in 500+ Sephora stores across 19 European countries. In Q1 Rhode contributed about $160M and 'outperformed our expectations', and total Q1 revenue of $479.4M beat a $425.7-428M consensus by about 12%. Consensus of $467-471M sits at the top of the guided band, not above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-08-05): revenue beat by about 12%, plus a raise, gave +6.88%. Q4 FY26 (2026-05-20) gave +4.73%. Q3 FY26 (2026-02-04): sales +38% with a raised outlook, and the stock fell 9.18% (https://rallies.ai/news/elf-beauty-beats-q3-eps-by-72-raises-full-year-revenue-outlook-by-42m50m). Revenue beats have been bought and sold depending on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Much of it is priced. Consensus already embeds mid-30s growth and the stock is up about 26% since the last print. What is not visible is the size of the Europe pipeline, which management never quantified, and whether it beat its own planning as Rhode did in Q1. If the market expected a large pipeline-driven beat, consensus would sit above $471M (the top of the guide) and the whisper revenue would be published above it; it is not. Lands inside guidance, so sized small.
findings.independence: Rhode Europe launch date and footprint from a separate company release (https://investor.elfbeauty.com/stock-and-financial/press-releases/landing-news/2026/08-31-2026-140024924). Shares a document (the Q1 call) with the guidance finding below. Pipeline is retailer stocking, not sell-through; the Earnings Whispers preview makes the same point (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand).

findings.finding: The FY27 guide leaves arithmetic room for a second raise. The $1,938-1,968M guide is +18-20%, which implies a FY26 base of about $1,642M. Prior-year quarters are Q1 $353.7M, Q2 $343.9M and Q3 $489.5M, so prior-year Q4 was about $455M. FY27 Q1 was $479.4M and Q2 is guided to about $464-471M. That leaves an implied H2 of about $990-1,020M, or +5% to +8% on a $945M prior-year H2, once Rhode is annualised (August). Management separately said organic growth for the balance of the year would be 10-12% and that 'all brands grow' (my derivation from the 2026-08-05 release and call). Last time the raise (+$100M of sales) exceeded the Q1 beat (about $50M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Raise in Aug 2026 gave +6.88%. FY27 first guide in May 2026 gave +4.73%. Raise in Feb 2026 gave -9.18%, sold on core-brand quality. The Nov 2025 guide disappointment gave -35.04%. Guidance is the line this stock trades on, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The H2 implied growth is a derived number that no preview I found computes. The Earnings Whispers preview says even a reaffirmation would push estimates higher, which implies FY consensus sits inside the range rather than above it. If a raise were fully priced, a published FY consensus would sit above $1,968M. The 26% run-up says some raise is expected; how big it is decides the print. The $50M refund reinvestment runs through Q2-Q4, so any EBITDA/EPS raise may be muted relative to sales.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-27, on the reaffirmation pushing estimates up (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand). Shares the company's Q1 document with the finding above; this one is about the forward guide, not the reported quarter.

findings.finding: A counterparty reading on the core e.l.f. brand points softer than management's 'improving trends'. Ulta reported its quarter ended 2026-08-01 on 2026-08-27, after e.l.f.'s last call. It said mass makeup sales declined in the low single digits as brands lapped big launches, and cosmetics fell to 37% of its sales from 38%. e.l.f. Cosmetics is the largest mass color brand. This overlaps only July of e.l.f.'s Sep quarter. Ulta is one channel, and management said e.l.f.'s fall innovation held 4 of the top 10 new launches in mass cosmetics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Core-brand weakness drove the large negatives: Nov 2025 -35.04% and Feb 2026 -9.18%, the latter despite a total-revenue beat (https://www.tipranks.com/news/e-l-f-beauty-stock-elf-plunges-as-intl-sales-slow-outlook-disappoints-wall-street describes the international and outlook reaction).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a proxy: one retailer, a category-level reading, and a period that overlaps one month of e.l.f.'s quarter. The market's attention is on Rhode and the run-up. If core-brand risk were priced the stock would not be at its 52-week high; the +27-point put skew may partly reflect it. Net of the rest of the company: core e.l.f. organic was guided to grow over the balance of the year and Rhode is now about a third of sales, so the core can miss slightly while the total still beats.
findings.independence: Ulta call highlights (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-ulta-beauty-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-27/). Earnings Whispers notes e.l.f. units fell about 3 points last quarter and calls the core brand the weaker link (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand). Against it: the company's own Q1 call cites improving scanner trends in units and dollars.

findings.finding: e.l.f. reversed its broad price-discovery test in August. About 90% of tested SKUs went back to pre-test prices 'over the next couple weeks' after 2026-08-05. Management said unit gains on those items 'just was not enough to justify the investment'. Only about 10% of SKUs stay at lower prices. So September-quarter unit volume on most of the e.l.f. line faces a price step-up versus July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Units fell about 3 points in Q1 while price and mix added 39 points, and the print gave +6.88% anyway. Unit softness has mattered when it reached the guide (Nov 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: This was public on the call, so mostly priced. The open question is elasticity on the restored prices, which management did not quantify. Previews discuss the 10% kept down, not the 90% restored. Inference, sized small.
findings.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 2. No independent scanner series for Aug-Oct 2026 was reachable.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is stretched. The stock is up about 26% since the 2026-08-05 report (Earnings Whispers, 2026-10-27), +11.96% over 20 days, and 0.59% below its 52-week high at $117.60. 25-delta put skew is +26.97 vol points, so the option market is paying for downside. The name sold a beat-and-raise in Feb 2026 (-9.18%). Four of its last six prints were negative, with a median absolute move of 9.33%. Short interest is not crowded: 7.4% of shares, 3.5 days to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two most recent prints, both beat-and-raise from depressed levels, gave +4.73% and +6.88%. The Feb 2026 beat-and-raise after a rebound gave -9.18%. The Nov 2025 print gave -35.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is not unpriced information. It sets the bar: after a 26% run to the high, a mid-30s print plus a modest raise is what is expected. The skew agrees with this sign, so the finding agrees with the market rather than against it, and it is sized accordingly. If the run-up had already been sold down, the stock would sit well off its high and the skew would have normalised.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline (skew, run-up, 52-week high). Short interest from https://massive.com/quote/elf (as of 2026-10-15). The sentiment shift from deeply bearish to mildly bearish is from the Earnings Whispers preview.

findings.finding: EPS bar is disputed, and Q2 carries the start of a $50M reinvestment. Management said the full $50M Q1 tariff refund is reinvested Q2-Q4, mostly in marketing. Marketing will run above the 23-25% range after Q1's 22% underspend, and balance-of-year adjusted EBITDA margins will be mid-teens. Published Q2 EPS consensus ranges from $0.34-0.35 (aggregators) to $0.58-0.61 (TipRanks, Earnings Whispers), against a $0.73 whisper. Front-loaded spend could produce an EPS figure that reads as a miss against the higher sources.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 EPS beat by $1.00 on the refund, and the stock gave +6.88%, a reaction smaller than the beat would suggest. EPS has not been the line this stock trades on; revenue, core-brand trend and guidance have.
findings.why_not_priced: Phasing by quarter was explicitly not given ('we really haven't broken that down by a quarter'), so the Q2 share of reinvestment is unknown to everyone. Capped small because the EPS bar is disputed.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers $0.61 and $0.73 whisper (https://finviz.com/news/409483/elf-beauty-faces-proof-test-as-rodes-european-launch-meets-a-soft-core-brand). Aggregator $0.34-0.35 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/ELF, https://www.opencapital.sh/stocks/elf/earnings/q2-2026). Same call document as findings 1, 2 and 4.

findings.independence: EDGAR filing list showing Form 144s on 2026-09-01, 09-08 and 10-01 and Form 4s through 2026-10-19 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001600033&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40).

findings.finding: Tariff cost on China-sourced product may still be in play after the IEEPA refunds. Section 301 duties on Chinese cosmetics remain in force. The status of the Section 122 replacement tariff after its about 150-day term is unclear in public sources. e.l.f. said about 60% of production will be outside China by the end of FY27. It said freight cost increases are already baked in, and that suppliers have not passed on new input-cost increases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff-driven margin cuts coincided with the Nov 2025 -35.04% print. The August 2025 print, which lowered the margin outlook on tariffs, gave -9.48%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a macro-to-company proxy that the company has not confirmed as a new headwind, and public tariff sources disagree. Management guided gross margin ex-refunds flat for FY27. Sized small.
findings.independence: Company statement on cost inflation and supply-chain shift, Q1 call (https://investor.elfbeauty.com/~/media/Files/E/ELF-IR/documents/event-and-presentation/elf-q1-fy27-earnings-call-transcript.pdf). That source cuts against the finding.

baseline_tension: The fundamental findings (pipeline-boosted Q2 and room for a guide raise) cut against the +27-point put skew. The positioning finding agrees with it. Net, the evidence is roughly balanced on a name priced for an 11.6% move.
lessons_applied: Rules 1 and 6 cut finding 1 (Q2 revenue beat) from +1.0 to +0.5: the finding lands inside the company's own mid-30s guide, and this name sold a 38% beat-and-raise in Feb 2026.
Rule 1 cut finding 2 (guide raise) from +1.5 to +1.2: the guidance line has paid in both directions on this name, and the reinvestment may mute an EPS raise.
print_vs_bar_pct trimmed from +3.0 to +2.5 because consensus already sits at the top of the guided band.
Rule 6 left the EPS finding capped at -0.3 because the EPS bar is disputed (two sources at $0.58-0.61 against two at $0.34-0.35). Already small in the draft; nothing else changed.
Rule 7 left positioning at -2.0: the sign agrees with the skew, and short interest (7.4%, 3.5 DTC) is not crowded, so no squeeze haircut was needed.
